R1854-P2.summary: Marriage negotiations reported through ser Vittorio and Giovanni de Orlandis: a countess agrees to the match of her daughter; the subjects object that the lord of Mantua is too far away and that 'Carolus est nimis iuvenis ad talia' (Carlo Gonzaga, b. 1417); Antonio Colonna and the cousins of domina Palma are mentioned.
R1854-P2.en:
Yesterday Giovanni de Orlandis, as soon as he saw me, told me that ser Vittorio had come to him that same day, saying
that the lady countess [wished] to do all that pleases [you], and the aforesaid Giovanni too. But because he was then
beginning to dine, he said he would come back to him and speak more fully on this matter. Afterwards, when yesterday
evening many of us were gathered in the house of the [cardinal] of Siena for an academic act and to dine with the
aforesaid [cardinal], while I was in the hall before dinner, behold, ser Vittorio — for he frequents the place,
because he has a son there — came up to me, and at length, after greeting me, he spoke many words, but in conclusion:
that last Thursday, coming from Calabria, he passed through Rome with a cousin of lady Palma, who was escorting his
own sister, married beyond Viterbo; from there he came back the day before;

system: Homophonic substitution in graphic signs and digits with about a dozen nulls, syllable signs for con, et and -rum, and two word codes (ARW = cardinalis).
